review_notes: I read the whole file. The main simp-relevant areas are the ElasticityAugmented algebra, the ElasticityParameter derivation API, and the ElasticityFrame projection lemmas. The file has no @[simp] lemmas, and I found no simp cycles or competing rules. Findings are about missing canonical simp lemmas, shown by repeated manual `simp only` lists and rfl side-lemmas. I checked that Mathlib's Subalgebra files (Basic.lean) have no numeral-coercion simp lemma (only `Subalgebra.coe_one`). I also checked that sibling files in the same project (Planar, Transfer, Variational) tag analogous `_apply` rfl lemmas with @[simp]. I could not run Lean. I did not check whether `Smooth` is `ElasticityAugmented.Smooth` defined elsewhere with its own simp set, and I did not verify that the proposed attributes cause no clashes in downstream files that import this one.

findings.excerpt: have h2 : ((2 : Smooth) : X → ℂ) x=(2 : ℂ) := rfl
findings.problem: The same rfl fact, that the coercion of the numeral `(2 : Smooth)` to a function evaluates to `(2 : ℂ)`, is re-proved as a local `have` in about six proofs (lines 859-860, 929, 1019, 1030, 1058, plus the same pattern in other files), each followed by a manual `rw [h2]`. No simp lemma handles the evaluation of a numeral element of `Smooth` at a point. The file also has no lemma for the coercion of `(2 : Smooth)` or `(4 : Smooth)` to a function. So each `simp only [Subalgebra.coe_mul, Pi.mul_apply, ...]` call stops at `((2 : Smooth) : X → ℂ) x`, which forces the manual rewrite. Mathlib has only `Subalgebra.coe_one`, so this is a project-level gap.
findings.proposed_change: Add once, next to `smoothInv_apply`, a simp lemma such as `@[simp] lemma coe_ofNat_apply (n : ℕ) [n.AtLeastTwo] (x : X) : (((OfNat.ofNat n : Smooth)) : X → ℂ) x = OfNat.ofNat n := rfl`. Drop the local `h2`/`h4` facts and the `rw [h2]` / `rw [h2,h4] at hh` steps. In each proof, `simp only [...]` can then include this lemma, or the proof can use plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: The numeral-evaluation fact is stated once and is used by simp automatically. This removes duplicated boilerplate, keeps the `simp only` sets focused, and makes `Smooth` coefficients with numerals normalise to `ℂ` numerals. That suits the `field_simp`/`linear_combination` steps that follow.

findings.excerpt:
lemma smoothInv_apply (f : Smooth) (hf : ∀ x, (f : X → ℂ) x≠0) (x : X) :
    (smoothInv f hf : X → ℂ) x=((f : X → ℂ) x)⁻¹ := rfl
findings.problem: This is the canonical pointwise evaluation lemma for `smoothInv`, in the normal form that field arithmetic wants (an `⁻¹` on `ℂ`). It is not tagged `@[simp]`, so it has to be added by hand to about ten `simp only` calls. Examples are `normal_form_top`, `transportT_eq`, `change_inverseS`, `inverse_changeS`, `leadingR_change` and `normal_form_bottom`. Sibling files in the same project tag exactly this kind of rfl `_apply` lemma `@[simp]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `smoothInv_apply` as `@[simp]`, as the project already does for `cut_apply`, `d_apply` and `cj_apply`. Then remove it from the explicit `simp only` lists. It is safe: the left side is a function application on a specific definition, the right side is smaller, and it cannot loop.
findings.benefit: The pointwise reduction of the inverse works uniformly under plain `simp`. It will not be forgotten in new proofs, and the long `simp only` lists get shorter.

findings.excerpt: lemma direction_mul (θ : Fin 3 → ℂ) (f g : Smooth) :
findings.problem: These are the Leibniz and linearity rules for `direction coord θ`. They are rewrite rules in the obvious direction, since the derivative is pushed to the arguments, and they terminate. None is tagged `@[simp]`. The file lists them by name in many `simp only [direction_mul, direction_add, direction_sum, direction_inv, ...]` calls. Examples are `normal_form_top`, `contraction_derivative`, `changeS_derivative` and `transformed_gradient`. The `direction (A := Smooth) coord θ` form also has no canonical relation to the `thetaDerivation θ` form beyond `thetaDerivation_apply`. Once a derivation-linearity lemma is missed, simp stalls on opaque `direction ...` terms.
findings.proposed_change: Either tag `direction_mul`, `direction_add`, `direction_smul` and `direction_sum` as `@[simp]`, or define a local simp set via `register_simp_attr` for them. Tag `thetaDerivation_apply` as `@[simp]` too, so the two spellings normalise to `direction`. Keep `direction_inv` as a conditional lemma, since it needs `hf` and is not clean for simp. The `simp only` lists then only need the problem-specific `changeP`/`changeS` unfoldings.
findings.benefit: Derivative expansion becomes automatic and consistent. Proofs such as `transformed_scalar` and `contraction_derivative` stop depending on hand-curated lists, and the `thetaDerivation`/`direction` spellings are no longer a source of simp failures.

findings.excerpt:
lemma delta_apply (v : E) (f : Smooth E) (x : E) :
    (delta v f : E → ℂ) x=fderiv ℝ (f : E → ℂ) x v := rfl
findings.problem: `delta_apply` is the canonical evaluation lemma for the derivation `delta`. It is `rfl`, but it is not a simp lemma. It is passed explicitly to `simp only` in `holomorphic_of_supported_transport`, where the `Subalgebra.coe_mul`/`Pi.mul_apply` lists are also spelled out by hand. The related `pbar_apply` is used only through `rw`. Without these, `simp` cannot see through `(delta v f : E → ℂ) x`, and users must remember the lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `delta_apply` as `@[simp]`, matching the `d_apply` convention in Planar.lean and Variational.lean. Optionally mark `characteristicPlane_one` and `characteristicPlane_I` as `@[simp]`. They are currently proved with `simp [characteristicPlane]`, so `characteristicPlane` is unfolded ad hoc, and the file then works with the named sums. The result is evaluation lemmas for `delta` and `characteristicPlane` instead of unfolding the definition.
findings.benefit: `simp` can evaluate `delta` and `characteristicPlane` consistently without exposing the `fderiv`/`reCLM.smulRight` implementation, and call sites such as `holomorphic_of_supported_transport` get shorter `simp only` sets.
